## Notes

### Quick read
- Emily is a sleek, Scandinavian-looking blonde toddler mom whose 3.5-year-old son (about 35 lbs) rides in her Leopard sling; clean, aesthetic, text-overlay content with a strong "save my arms" angle.
- Best next move: reply to her unanswered Sep 22 question about the revision (she already fixed it herself and the new cut was approved Sep 22), thank her, and hand her ideas; she has been waiting on slow reviews and is a little frustrated.

### Style (from watching her videos)
- Who she is on camera: mom, long platinum blonde hair, minimal makeup, matching burgundy sweatsuit, calm and model-like. One son, 3.5 years old, around 35 lbs, dark hair, red and grey outfit. Settings: outdoor steps of a modern townhouse, then a plain grey wall indoors (studio-like, clean). Sling is Leopard.
- Format: text-overlay b-roll with a voiceover, calm and minimal, 25 to 28s. Structure: carrying him on her hip (the problem), show the empty sling on, put him in, close up of the padded shoulder strap and buckle, him cuddled in.
- Hooks (quote): "If your toddler still wants to be carried everywhere, but your arms and back are done, this has been a game-changer."; overlays "when your toddler still wants to be carried...", "35 lbs of toddler 👀", "padded shoulder strap", "he gets the cuddles, I save my arms 🤍".
- What worked: 25f526ff approved Sep 22 (not yet run). She resubmitted after removing "any clips where I'm not supporting the sling".
- What got rejected: 68f1b867 (Sep 12), no review comment; she saw it as a revision request with no feedback. From the frames the likely issue was moments without a hand on him.
- Safety and checklist issues seen:
  - Both cuts open on outdoor steps holding her son (1s). The checklist says no stairs; he does not look to be in the sling yet at that moment, but it is still a stairs shot.
  - 25f526ff: hand under his leg or at his back in the frames with him in the sling; seat under his bottom; buckle closed (close up at 18s). Good.
  - 35 lbs is inside the 10 to 50 lbs range. She states it as a weight, which is exactly right.
- Strengths to lean on: the heavy toddler angle (35 lbs, 3.5 years) that most creators cannot show; clean, premium aesthetic; accurate weight language.
- To improve: skip the stairs opener; show her own face talking for one version (she has presence).
